chunks: From him, from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān ibn Rushayd, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Yūnus, from Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr ibn Sām, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Thieves are three: the one who withholds zakat (alms-tax), the one who deems lawful the dowries of women, and likewise the one who incurs a debt and does not intend to repay it.”

key_terms.مَانِعُ الزَّكَاةِ: one who withholds the obligatory zakat (alms-tax)
key_terms.مُسْتَحِلُّ مُهُورِ النِّسَاءِ: one who treats women’s dowries as lawful to consume without right

ai.seo_question: Which actions are described as forms of theft in this hadith of Imām al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith identifies certain forms of wrongful appropriation as theft, even when they may not appear as ordinary stealing. It condemns withholding zakat (alms-tax), unlawfully consuming women’s dowries, and taking on debt without intending repayment as serious moral and legal violations against the rights of others.
